ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, the graph of the quadratic function $y=ax^{2}+bx-3$ intersects the $x$-axis at points $A(-1,0)$ and $B(3,0)$, and intersects the $y$-axis at point $C$. The vertex of the parabola is point $M$. What is the analytical expression of the quadratic function?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Substitute point A ($-1$, $0$) and point B ($3$, $0$) into $y=ax^{2}+bx-3$,\\
we get $\begin{cases}a-b-3=0\\ 9a+3b-3=0\end{cases}$.\\
Solving this, we find $\begin{cases}a=1\\ b=-2\end{cases}$.\\
Therefore, the equation of the quadratic function is $\boxed{y=x^{2}-2x-3}$.
